forms.pokedex_entry: Kiweaf are natural-born troopers, refusing to give up even in the worst-circumstances. They use their bush to hide amongst the forest floor.
The leaf on its head is surprisingly resiliant, allowing it to headbutt foes. Able to synthesize energy from the sun, Ostroop can march on for hours.
Armazoura's leaves have grown into an impenetrable armor, able to shrug off the most devastating hits. It was once used to guard members of royalty.
Flaigos tend to be overconfident, ramming head first into various situations. The grass it eats fuels its smokey mane.
This rebellious Pokemon requires lots of food to sustain is speedy metabolism. A simple whiff of its neck gas can lead to difficulty breathing.
Miasmeras uses its toxic fumes and false-headed tail to strike fear into its enemies. It was once used as a weapon of war for its sheer brutality.
Due to their squishy bodies, Snessel use relic vessels to protect themselves. While agile in water, this creates difficulty moving on land.
To limit visual distractions, Shelphore wears broken pottery over its eyes. It stands upright on its tail when using its psychic powers.
When focused, Kratericle can predict the most minute decisions its opponent makes. It was once revered for its ability to forsee the future.
Vermet stash food and trinkets in their fluffy tails. Their tails puff up when startled, however, so many of these items are often lost to a simple scare.
They wrap their tails around other Minurrel for support as they dig, using their metal claws like pickaxes. Its eyes can detect rare ores beneath the earth.
Notoriously chatty, it uses a variety of whistles to signal for food or warn others of danger. Its long legs are built to run along the vast shores of the region.
It sings and capers along mudflats and shores to rile up prey hidden beneath the surface. Kelpish and Gravvorm are some of its favorite morsels to find.
It dances gracefully through the sky, as if it's walking along the air. Witnessing such a display is believed to bring good fortune for a lifetime.
It sleeps in shallow waters using its tail as a snorkel, while its heavy amber collar keeps its head submerged. At night, it emerges to feed on tree sap.
Casquito hang motionless on trees and cave ceilings awaiting evolution. If parts of their amber coating chips off, Ambug help repair it.
It now has enough amber to withstand the sun. While it usually eats resin, it has been known to steal grapes from Spoink, often becoming too tipsy to fly.
Corypillar is not actually crying, its tear-like appendages just help garner attention. It naps in flowers petals after it has had its fill of nectar.
Jackoon is still developing proper limbs, so it lacks balance. Despite this, it seems to enjoy the delight of onlookers witnessing its clumsy nature.
Claudifly loves to pull pranks and juggle the pollen puffs on its head. Many people find their antics annoying, but some find them quite charming.
Its body is so light that even a small breeze can cause it to drift away for miles. It absorbs air particles in order to evolve.

The sea salt in the air of southern Fusis caused Nimbim to evolve into this form of Aneminal. It can freely manipulate the water that makes up its body.
The ice crystals in the air of western Fusis caused Nimbim to evolve into this form of Aneminal. It can freely manipulate the snow that makes up its body.
The sediments in the air of eastern Fusis caused Nimbim to evolve into this form of Aneminal. It can freely manipulate the sand that makes up its body.
The irritants in the air of northern Fusis caused Nimbim to evolve into this form of Aneminal. It can freely manipulate the pollen that makes up its body.
Feathal are aggressive and territorial, protecting their hunting grounds at all costs. They fling metallic feathers at foes who get too close.
It can solidify the liquid metal of its wings to slash at prey and volley darts at its foes. Kids are taught to seek shelter if they hear its cry nearby.
Legend has it, Spirdix are the souls of those who have fallen to their doom. They fly and nest low to the ground, supposedly wary of falling again.
The gem on its chest glows when it is facing north. Sailors thought of them as deities, following their flight when the stars were covered by clouds.
A bashful Pokemon, it clings to branches with its vines to avoid trouble. Groups of them create delightful bell-like chimes in the forest breeze.
This tender-hearted Pokemon is used by nurses across the region. Simply hearing the chime of its flower bells can alleviate years of chronic aches and pains.
It ferments the wild grapes it consumes by bouncing, creating a potent toxin. This has numbed its psychic power, but keeps predators away.
Grumpig stomps grapes and berries it finds into a sweet tasting fluid that dulls the senses. Its dance is more disorderly than its Hoennian cousin.
Swionysus’s tail stores grapes and berries for snacking as it lounges. Any forgotten berries ferment into fine wines that are sold across the region.
A rambunctious and playful Pokémon, it often prances around the forest and uses sticks to play fight with other Fawnee.
The sharp growth on its arm is used to carve into trees in order to mark its territory. Despite their vigor, they only sleep three hours at a time.
Amazentars were once used by warriors to ride into battle. One back kick from this robust Pokémon can decimate an entire brick wall.
Unsuspecting travelers will sit atop its head, mistaking it for ruinous stone. A layer of lichen covers the last standing element of a forgotten empire.
Endoric does not eat. Instead, it melts small rocks with its caustic lichen arms and absorbs their minerals to strengthen its own body.
The toxic endolith in its body acts like a set of powerful muscles. While normally placid, Lycorinth will rampage if it finds any vandalism in its home ruins.
Swipus uses its strange card to deceive humans and Pokémon. If its card is ever lost or ruined, it grows depressed until it finds a replacement.
The guilt from its misdeeds is said to be the cause of Supuleist's black fur falling out. It stays in denial, using this shed fur as a cloak to continue swindling.
Fuzzeu crawls along frozen cave walls and ceilings. It is often a carrier of the common cold, unknowingly infecting humans and other Pokémon.
Underneath its thick fur and gruesome demeanor hides a gentle heart. Beware, however! Just one lick of its tongue can cause severe frostbite.
Initially deemed a Combee variant, it was reclassified due to an inability to detect bug pheromones. Instead it emits sound from its ears to communicate.
It ruthlessly orders swarms of Combeat to do its bidding using high-pitched frequencies. Its tail chamber can blast sound as loud as 125 decibels.
Wooper have been chased off by predators in the swamps. They now live in icy caves, obtaining moisture from the crystals that stick to its face.
Quagsire's rocky crest and body are coated with frozen slime, making solid hits difficult. It remains about as dim-witted as it's Johtonian cousin.
The ice-glazed rock on Kraggsire's body make for the perfect offense and defense. Woopers often cling to its back as it belly slides through caves.
After being brought to Mount Kion, Dwebble began to make homes from nearby snow and ice. It spits a fluid that makes snow easier to ball up.
Frostle's claws are made to plow snow with the utmost ease. It is known to house Dwebble in its shell when fresh packing snow becomes scarce.
When Kittoo is scared, frost-covered back fur spikes up. You can tell how it is feeling by looking at the position of its whiskers.
The underbelly of a Himalion stores mass amounts of static electricity. It uses electroreception to find prey during blizzards, when visibility is near zero.
Olympuma is too slow to hunt. Instead it hides in the snow, waiting to shock any prey unlucky enough to pass by. Its fur creates beautiful auroras.
These Pokémon live in the murky allies of cities, raiding any trash bins they find. The influence of particularly devious Pokémon causes them to evolve.
This evolution was influenced by the cunning of the Supuleist line. Its bone sword is used to defend itself and slice open trash bags for scavenging.
It uses rotational force to generate electricity. The horn on its head delivers painful shocks to any threat in its path.
When it rains, Boltread will race towards the nearest storm cloud to gather electricity. Small children love to sit atop its head and hitch a ride.
Electricity fills the air as it recklessly drifts across open trails and roadways. It apparently looked quite different before the Industrial Era.
Kelpish swim along the water's surface to absorb sunlight. This makes it vulnerable to predators, so it stays close to kelp forests to blend into.
Lamigill can contort its flat body to slip through small cracks and crevices. It's cellular structure is actually more akin to plants oddly enough.
Filfurr is often teased for its carelessness and scruffy appearance. It takes mud baths to cool off, but it's unable to get rid of the dirt and gravel.
Pampurr are highly regarded in Pokémon contests and beauty paegants. They are also kindhearted, often cleaning up dirty Pokémon with their tail.
Snoopup are very nosy Pokémon, thouroughly investigating any strange sounds or smells. The paw-like pattern on its ears glow in the dark.
Its sense of smell is unrivaled, and its hearing is not far behind. It's even able to visually materialize scent trails and footprints with its psychic abilities.
The feet of a Boomba release a strong pulse, accentuating every step it takes. For whatever reason, it has a strange affinity for discs, like TMs.

Duraboom carries its bulky frame on hefty arms. It is said to “think in rhythm,” matching its opponent’s tempo to counterattack with precision.

Formidiboom is so proud of its voice, it blares victory tunes after winning a battle. Young and cocky trainers use it as a finisher Pokemon for this reason.

When a charm is cursed with bad luck, a Euseemi is born. If it senses impurity within your soul, it will follow you around and haunt you forever.
Try not to stare at this Pokémon, as tainted souls that gaze upon its eye are cursed for years. It can detach its arms to shoot optical beams of energy.
Many children adore this Pokémon for its docile nature and warm velvet belly. They are used in old fashioned theatres to provide lighting effects.
It can absorb and transfer the vitality of people and Pokémon. On warm nights, they approach humans in hopes of getting rare candy to grow stronger.
It generates its own healing energy, giving it to those in need. There is a notable story about a wounded hiker being saved by its kindness.
The Reaper Cloth has warped its physiology. Mortreaper's own vitality drains constantly, forcing it to absorb the life force of others.
It likes to mimic the poses of humans, by manipulating shadows. Nobody is really sure if the mask it has is its true face or if something else lies beneath it...
It can take multiple forms depending on its mood. Make sure to smile and applaud for its performances, unless you want to be cursed!
Mastasma takes on this form in times when it is overjoyed. This positivity escapes its body in the form of erratic electricity.
Mastasma takes on this form in times when it is furious. This anger escapes its body in the form of wrathful flames.
Mastasma takes on this form in times when it is gloomy. This sorrow escapes its body in the form of rushing waves.
It moves underground by eating straight through dirt and stone. When it rains, their heads are often seen poking above the surface.
This nocturnal Pokémon slinks about in local cemeteries, tormenting any graverobbers that manage to sneak in. It has a grip strength of 900 psi.
Geothermal hotspots in Fusis gave rise to this form of Mudbray. It's stubborn and lazy but once it gets moving, its body heat increases immensely.
The scalding hot lava in Mudsdale's mane is used to seal cracks in stoneware. Its molten hooves scorch the ground beneath it as it gallops.
A distant relative of Nacli, groups of Mudbray will follow it to lick its salty body. Grubble doesn't seem to mind, as the heat they emit staves off moisture.
Using centripetal force, it knocks back foes with its oversized arm. During a heatwave, their unique aroma will fill the air with the smell of grilled meat.
Anyone that dares cross it must yield to its massive arms and tremendous appetite. Five-star restaurants have its delicious salt to thank for their status.
Unlike females, males can inflate their dewlaps to guard from attacks or challenge rival males. Surprisingly strong, it can lift 5x its own weight.
Females have longer and more dexterous tails than males. They're useful for clinging onto branches and can even detatch in an emergency.
They can inflate and fill their muscles with significant power. One punch from a fully-inflated Swolizar can turn a large boulder into dust.
It uses its long, springy tail to perform stunning acrobatic feats. It takes down large opponents with style and captures prey with utmost grace.
It traveled with its herd using a psychic link to avoid getting lost. Pokémon like Drowzee, Munna and Phanpy share Telephant as a common ancestor.
Few predators could breach its psionic barriers; it likely died out during an ice age. Interestingly, Life Orbs are only found in the same regions its fossils lie.
It is the ancestor of simian Pokémon like Chimchar and Darumaka. Primite was quite intelligent, but far too slow of a learner to survive extinction.
It's believed to link humans and Pokémon, but doubts persist. Revived ones are smart but often have tantrums and emit ear smoke when puzzled.
Ueffohm used electrical signals to communicate with its species in the past. Their fossils are only found near old meteor impact zones, so they're quite rare.
Ohmvieni could create its own orbit using its electromagnetism. It is one of the few Pokémon able to survive within the cold vacuum of space.
One of the most gullible Pokémon, it is loyal to almost anyone. They are known to uncover priceless fossils only to bury them again.
More intelligent than Fossyle, wild Gilackee often act as minions for their pack leader. It always follows orders, no matter the cost.
Wild Tyralpha are cruel rulers over the younger members of its species. It's not uncommon for Fossyle and even Gilackee to seek shelter with kind trainers.
Harpuni invades nests, hogging food for other hatchlings. Its lightweight fluff lets it ride air currents as its wings develop.
Harplume's wing flaps are completely silent. This allows it to easily swoop in on prey or steal the trinkets of passersby during nightfall.
A chill in the air often marks Harpocalyps’s presence. Superstition claims that coming across even a single one of its feathers is a bad omen.
Trainers are often left with disappointment when a free Poké Ball they find along the ground turns out to be a timid Godda in disguise.
Kachimoll possess a surprising amount of power, but typically stay withdrawn unless they're in danger. Why it resembles a Poké Ball remains unclear.
If Kachimoll faces too much pressure, it opens up its shell and goes on the offensive. Its four sturdy tentacles can snap a telephone pole in half.
Volcuttle shoots a bright, scalding liquid for defense. It glows beautifully, but be wary! Its hot mantle causes the water around it to boil in seconds.
It sits on the ocean floor, capturing anything that moves with its many tentacles. It boils its prey before consuming it for easy digestion.
After being raised on sugar-filled crops, its lava has become sweet and sticky. It can be a nusciance, however, as Bug-Pokémon are drawn to its smell.
Kamerupt is used to transport goods across the vast desert. The sweetness of its lava has magnified upon evolution and is used in many pastries.
Its body is so rigid that it needs to wobble back and forth in order to move. If one falls over, it is sadly subject to the wills of Termydon.
Long ago, a giant replica of Spartallion filled with soldiers was used to successfully invade a city. It has been a symbol of victory ever since.
Forged as guardians, Autaloton are powered by ichor, a fluid of unknown origin. The screws in their bodies keep their volatile cores in check.
When its screws come loose, Autaloton’s blue core is unleashed. In this state, it releases icy winds capable of freezing an entire lake over.
When its screws come loose, Autaloton’s yellow core is unleashed. In this state, it generates electrical currents that could power an entire factory.
When its screws come loose, Autaloton’s red core is unleashed. In this state, it spews molten flames that can turn entire forests into ashes.
Termydon collect fresh wood and even cloth fibers to eat and share with its colony. Swingallop and Raghoul despise it greatly for this reason.
Myrmortar's abdomen can produce flames hot enough to melt through solid steel. It blasts colony invaders with great speed and precision.
Myrmantle's exoskeleton can withstand the force of a bomb, point blank. It builds walls and tunnels for its colony and guards their entrances.
Myrmach's wings allow it to hover and pivot midair. It is always on the move, hastily locating food, territory or potential danger for the colony.
A lively individual, it faces off against other Fisword with its dagger-like nose. It sharpens its nose against rocks after every battle.
Xivateer wields its blade-tipped nose with great speed and ferocity, slicing anything in its path. It often leads a group of Fisword called a crew.
Sailors who die at sea supposedly become this Pokémon. It sinks deep below the surface to feed on organic matter along the seabed.
Charonaut is said to ferry lost souls back to the afterlife. It seems unafectted by the ocean's immense pressure, no matter how deep it goes.
It enjoys the presence of humans, cheerily blowing bubbles from its blowhole at the sight of one. It emits sonar from its large head in order to navigate.
It expels excess salt water from its blowhole in the form of beautiful fountains. The serene sound of its voice lull all who hear it—including its prey.
This adorable Pokémon hides in coral reefs, using its shell for protection. Mollador pearls are highly valued by jewelers who make necklaces.
A layer of mucus keeps Clamorous's skin healthy and radiant. Its pretty shells are also quite hardy, capable of deflecting the shot of a harpoon.
It emits irresistable pheromones from its shell to lure in prey. In rare cases, predators have fallen under its sway and become its body guard
In ancient times it was thought Nytinyte were shooting stars fallen to earth. Individually, Nytinyte's pyschic abilities are rather weak.
Clusters of Nytinyte were thought to create a celestial being of power. When brought together, the sum of their psychic strength is great.
The toxins that Elixie produces were often used in medicine. This practice was dropped due to their many hallucinogenic side effects.
Sorcirix emits a beautifully scented mist to lure prey right to it. Rumor has it that any humans that happen to be lured in transform into Pokémon.
When enraged, its body becomes a jagged mass of crude oil that reeks of despair. When elated, its body becomes a smooth, fragrant oil that elicits hope.
While sunbathing, Slowcoco's leaves attract various Pokemon to try and nip at it. Despite the uncanny resemblance, it's unrelated to Slowpoke.
The freezing-cold bite of a Fuzzeu caused its leaves to become minty. It is very chill and often spaces out, much like its bizarre doppelganger—Slowbro.
The burning-hot bite of a Volcuttle, caused its leaves to become spicy. Its vast intellect and curiosity rivals that of its strange doppelganger—Slowking.
Toxins from the murky waters it feeds in accumulate in its spurs. It can launch them to defend itself, but they take time to regenerate.
It anchors itself in marsh soil to withstand rushing currents as it filter-feeds. Any predator strong enough to uproot it must face its toxic limbs.
It gulps down fertile wetland muck, absorbing its nutrients and water. Any filth and sediment leftover becomes ammo for its arm revolvers.
Turtoma's shell acts like a second set of jaws, clamping down on predators who try to sneak up on it. It wriggles its limbs to attract prey.
Making the most of its frightening shell maw, it can swim backwards as well as it does forwards. Despite its crushing strength, one hand can keep its maw shut.
It is thought that Tyrogue in Fusis gained their new typing after pleasing the gods. They compete in various athletics to determine the most worthy.
It is the fastest Pokémon in the region, leaving skid marks everywhere it runs. It needs to eat up to five times its own body weight to stay energized.
It can hit any target with pinpoint accuracy. One was recorded to have thrown its lightning bolt across nearly half the width of the Fusis region.
Left alone, it risks being hunted by predators like Guatro and Hypnotiss. It combusts and launches into the air in a pinch, signaling its parents.
It's size, strength and intellect make it an excellent taxi Pokemon. They burst into flames at high speeds, however, so taxi carriages must be fireproof.
Whether day or night, it is common to see sparring matches between Skrapion. Weights are grown on their bodies to develop their strength.
Able to crawl across the desert sands at impossible speeds, the punch of a Scorperior can turn sand into glass.
Ancient Fusians believed that the world was created by a Rubeetle that rolled the stars together. Its gem sparkles like the sun.
It wields an otherworldly physical power thought to be gifted to it by the gods. Scaroah are revered for their intellegence and strength.
Their band-like webs provide protection but inhibit movement. Found typically in dark areas, Wrapling's glowing eyes scare off any potential threats.
This Pokémon emits a dark aura that unsettles all who come across it. Those who resonate with Awrapaneid's energy have great success in training it.
Food served by a Crokeerie is delicious, but never tastes the same again. Its body emits a similar spectral frequency to Sinistea, suggesting a relation.
Much like the plate on its head, any drink poured from its chalices tastes immaculate. It is quite amicable too, often seen in restaurants helping waiters.
These enigmatic Pokémon stare blankly into the sun all day. They try to pick on Skrapion during their fights, but often end up having to flee.
Andosinx tend to rear up on their hind legs for intimidation. They crawl into ruins at night but enter into conflict with Awrapaneid.
When a Striangylar meets eyes with a Scaroah, a practically endless staring contest ensues, as they both take pride in guarding ruins and have mystical powers.
Hypnotiss sways its body to the rhythm of its flute, lulling foes into a trance. Unknowing travelers may mistake its coiled body for a woven basket.
Its cheek sacs can absorb and interact with virtual data, so developers use it to improve software. It is commonly infected with Pokérus.
An electrical impulse triggered the toxins in its body, causing an evolution. It cleverly phases through cyberspace, corrupting any software it touches.
A single, lively current flows through its body, allowing it to paralyze prey it coils around. It playfully nips at anything it finds with its plug-like fangs.
When its two heads work in tandem, it can release a steady surge of power. If they quarrel, however, its attacks weaken from uneven energy flow.
Its three heads generate a continuous flow of electricity. When they strike in unison, the resulting thunderclap can be heard for miles.
They use electricity to deter bird Pokémon away from the foliage they eat. Using radio waves, they send each other signals from afar.
Giradio pick up all sorts of radio signals across the region. They like tuning into song stations as they browse; each one has its own musical tastes.
It seems to be manmade, yet the secret to its creation has not been deciphered. It was used in naval battles because the flames they spit float on water.
If you encounter a Mosskus in the woods, befriend it. There is purified water stored within its mossy fur, making it a safe way to avoid thirst.
This nocturnal Pokémon has odd regenerative properties. Able to regrow limbs, snare traps are nothing more than a minor annoyance to Cerynoct.
Notoriously grumpy, Darquill can be rather challenging to bond with. They'll shoot off their poison tipped quills at anyone that perturbs them.
Skoulago collect only the prettiest of stones to hang from their ears. Although useful offensively, they prefer to keep them in pristine condition.
It secretes a foul irritant to deter most foes from crops it finds. As such, its ironclad elytra is mainly put to the test by Akrivace, who can stomach the smell.
When it leaps, its body resembles a draconic maw. This frightens most from the crops it claims, but Pentacade is unfazed by this display, forcing the two to clash.
Neoladl trots along the waterside at dusk to hunt for Nytinyte. It uses psychic power to extend its reach, scooping them up before they cluster together.
While normally gentle, Megaladl will magnify its paws with dark energy and pummel anyone who harms its Neoladl without hesitation.
Lyrphedy's mournful tunes drain its listeners of any hope. The melodies it strums only evoke joy around a Rodicee it has known for some time.
Rodicee’s fruits are normally bitter and sap vitality. In the presence of a Lyrpheus it trusts, however, they grow sweet and nourishing.
It often disguises itself as a beggar to trick people for food. The steel spines along its neck jab anyone who exposes its ruse, letting it flee.
It channels psychic energy through its metallic fur, firing sharp arrows from its tail. These arrows, much like itself, can also be cloaked by illusions.
Its flight capabilities are lacking so it uses its long feather to sense danger around it. How it evolves changes wildly depending on its gender.
Matrivoni pair for life
Its back pattern differs from Bronzor in Sinnoh, yet it remains just as peculiar. When it resonates, people and Pokémon nearby grow agitated and cannot sit still.
Brongong was brought to countless battles for its ability to invigorate entire armies. It strikes its own body to create powerful sonic blasts.
A barrel of cheese aged so long, it achieved enlightenment, becoming a Pokémon. Despite its stench, the cheese it produces is quite delicious.
Their poison is so strong, a single bite can knock out an Incredibull. Ironically, that same poison is also the main ingredient in many different medicines.
Lopharmak is capable of spontaneously creating remedies out of its own venom, which it shares with allies. Its twin tails are the symbol of medicine.
It oddly resembles Drampa, but its biology is more akin to a flower than a dragon. Its petals have an irresistible scent that can hypnotize almost anyone.
It is unrelated to Turtonator due to its thick fur and lack of a weak spot on its belly. It digs pits to trap and consume any Dwebble that skitter by.
Oftentimes, Nymfrost gather in large groups to dance with one another. They're able to skate along almost any surface as if it were ice.
Nymflurry erect ice palaces to rule over, freezing anyone who dares to enter their domain. The secret to their speed is hidden by mist.
Razclops engage in snowball fights to see who's the strongest. They will not hesitate to group up and pummel anyone that ruins their fun.
It will take over entire cave systems with their posse of Razclops. Although its one eye can be quite intimidating, it cannot percieve depth very well.
They live in the woods and protect its inhabitants. Folktales suggest that Pagelf imbue the wood they use for armor with magical properties.
It is known to be a chivalrous and astute fighter. However, it throws all honor and caution aside when it comes to facing its nemesis—Forterror.
It spreads out its flag-like wings when it has claimed territory or successfully defeated its archrival, Pagelf. Its fire attacks are fueled by its rage.
Though flightless, its wings are useful for protection and intimidation. The scales it sheds are used for construction due to their strength.
Its tail contains toxic glands, which it gnaws on to transfer poison into its 8-sided head crystal. This improves its odds against a deadly foe.
Lizorozil’s crystal—now 10-sided—contains poison that varies greatly in potency. Its false-headed tail and shifty nature protect its true head from danger.
Azuray effortlessly glides across the water surface. It's rather awkward on land, however, so trainers must ensure its skin and gills stay moist.
Amparay can sense the electrical impulse of other creatures. As such, predators have a hard time finding it, while prey find it difficult to flee.
Mantacular is swift both in the air and underwater, easily outspeeding a jet ski. Its tail can deliver shocks that leave foes paralyzed for weeks.
Its towering shell emits bizarre echoes that distort and amplify sounds around it. These unique soundwaves can even mimic human voices.
Kirtoot's stripes are able to shift into many hues for camoflauge. Their long tongue and goofy cries inspired the creation of noise makers.
Raveleon's mere presence is said to bring great joy to those around it. It is known to celebrate even the most mundane tasks its trainer accomplishes.
Eggon are truly helpless Pokémon. Their only form of protection are the eggshells they keep from birth. They have a knack for rare minerals.
These Pokémon are incredibly prideful, commanding over other Pokémon by showing off their extravagant feathers. This fails miserably.
Despite its immense power, Empeggon has other Pokémon bring it food and trinkets. It is greedy and lax, but treats its underlings quite well.
Chumprey latch onto larger marine Pokémon and drain their blood to get by. Too weak to fight, it constantly wishes to get stronger.
Chumprey latch onto larger marine Pokémon and drain their blood to get by. Too weak to fight, it constantly wishes to get stronger.
Monstrom's whirpools have been feared by seafarers since ancient times. Sunken ships and debris are commonplace within its underwater lair.
Monstrom's whirpools have been feared by seafarers since ancient times. Sunken ships and debris are commonplace within its underwater lair.
It drums its head with its trunk, which serves to signal its herd. However, these sounds may attract the attention of a hungry Slobbrrgen instead.
Drummoth use their rhythmic beats to commune with others. However, they often get carried away by the groove, inadvertently causing avalanches.
Timpannibal orchestrates its herd with a commanding drumbeat, impervious to even the harshest blizzards. It always knows a way back home.
Baaronze's wool is highly prized for its soft texture and exceptional durability. However, their numbers have dwindled greatly as a result.
It fortifies itself with thick, silvery wool as it prepares to evolve once more. Its final form depends on how well it can withstand various hardships.
Smaller Pokémon of the forest look to Golkauram for shelter. Its golden wool has healing properties that are the topic of many ancient myths.
Even the boldest Pokémon steer clear of Pterribex. Ancient myths speak of its phantom wool, glowing green with the souls of its prey.
Its exudes a revitalizing aura, bringing a sense of rebirth to all. It weaves a precious silk that is thought to herald new beginnings.
Its long body is in constant motion, said to measure the passage of time itself. Its toxins mirror life's challenges: potent but short-lived.
Its claws sever the very threads that bind souls to the mortal realm. Though feared, it only wishes to aid those who have reached their final hour.
It guards the secrets of its own prison, the Labyrinth. Ancient texts speak of Destrox's malice, but some say it only yearns for a companion.
Said to be the soul of an ancient soldier, it can never escape the confines of its shackles. It seeks out other Hekatone to fuse with and grow stronger.
Now shaped as gauntlets, its strikes can wound the soul. One of the pair is inverted, allowing for unorthodox fighting techniques
Its arms extend for distant attacks, and the eyes within its gauntlets track enemies effortlessly. Wisps of pure resentment churn along its head.
It is the strongest its shackles allow, emitting a pressure that burdens all nearby. Despite comprising countless Hekatone, they never bicker and act as one.
Apolithon's tendrils exude an aura that tarnishes the will of people and Pokémon. Its bronze has been forged into artifacts of immense power.

forms.display_name: Apolithon — King of All Things Tarnished
forms.pokedex_entry: After amassing enough strength, it brought about the Devastation of Fusis. Rare depicitons of this form called it ‘The King of All Things Tarnished.’
This Ultra Beast uses its watery mirrors to peer into alternate realities and open up wormholes. The Triad of Destiny seem to view it as their master.
Rumors speak of Flutyr's domain, The Beyond, a vast wilderness untouched by time. It plays melodies that reawaken the joys of childhood.
Clad in high-tech armor made by a deranged inventor, it makes up for its lack of speed with great bulk and overwhelming sound.
Supposedly born from the prayers of the helpless, it shroud itself in storm clouds and saved Fusis from utter destruction long ago.
